Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0006] Read existing modules to match error conventions: Before implementing, inspect errors.py and sibling modules to reuse the project's BillingError codes and helper functions.
  Explore the repo's error class and existing functions first; reuse established error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers rather than inventing new ones. This keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0002] Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.
- [rb-0003] Read the existing test file before implementing: Locating and reading the relevant test file (tests/test_average_unit_price.py) alongside models.py and money.py clarified expected types and behavior before writing code.
  Before editing, cat the target module, its models, its money helpers, and any test file matching the feature name. This reveals signatures, Decimal usage, and edge cases, enabling a first-attempt pass.
- [rb-0004] Reject bool as int for integer validation: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bool when validating positive integers.
  When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.
- [rb-0005] Normalize money inputs before sign checks: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
  Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the stored result before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Team convention requires every balance-changing operation to accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event>)` for a matching key and return the original result (including the stored record) without re-applying. Do this before state checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status has changed.

item.title: Enforce approval thresholds for large refunds
item.description: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver via keyword-only `approved_by=None`, raising BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
item.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is falsy. Keep the parameter keyword-only with a default so existing callers keep working, and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.

item.title: Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing a stub
item.description: Before writing a new function, read sibling modules (payments, audit, clock, money, errors) to reuse their helpers and error style.
item.content: The accepted implementation reused `to_money`/`round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, `BillingError` from errors, and `audit.record` for the audit trail. Matching existing conventions (rounding, error codes, audit event naming) is what made the diff pass hidden tests.
